newsitem.title: USA: Currencies not a major focus of G7 finmin talks.
newsitem.headline: Currencies not a major focus of G7 finmin talks.

text.p: Finance Ministers from the Group of Seven discussed currency markets at their meeting here but it was not a major focus, a senior U.S. Treasury Department official said.
"It certainly was not a major focus," the official, who declined to be named, told reporters.
In a statement to be issued shortly, G7 leaders barely mentioned currency rates, limiting their remarks to calling on their finance ministers to cooperate closely in foreign exchange markets.
In April the G7 finance ministers opposed excessive volatility in currency markets and said currency rates should reflect economic fundamentals and not lead to large trade imbalances.
Asked why Saturday's statement did not follow the same line, the U.S. official said it was a statement of the G7 leaders, not their finance ministers.

In their statement, the G7 leaders welcomed efforts by the European Union to forge a single currency under economic and monetary union (EMU) but stressed that it must be backed up by sound economic policies.
The leaders' statement did not specifically mention the planned 1999 start of EMU. The U.S. Treasury official said that timing was up to Europe to decide.
He did say that Europe must not allow EMU to divert it from structural economic reforms, budget deficit reduction and enlargement of the European Union.
The Treasury official also said that Japan needed to avoid a substantial and sustained rise in its current account surplus that could hurt the world economy.
He denied that the U.S. was backpedalling from its earlier criticism of Japan on trade.
